comment: Every place this package's ESLint config deliberately differs from @mnaoumov/typescript-dev-toolkit's shared config, and why.
`scripts/eslint-config.ts` is a HAND COPY of that config rather than a call of its `defineEslintConfigs`, and a
hand copy drifts silently, which it did for eighteen months. update-npm-deps.ps1 compares the two configs on every
dependency sweep, resolving the shared one from this package's own installed toolkit, and fails on anything not
The comparison is DIRECTIONAL: only 'the shared config refined something and this copy never took it' is a
finding. A rule this package enables that the shared config turns off is printed as information and never fails,
because this copy is then the stricter one and the shared config's reasons for its own relaxations are
measurements about the trees it was written for.
A key is the finding's identity exactly as the check prints it: <role>|<rule>|<kind>[|<detail>]. The
correspondence runs BOTH ways - an entry describing a divergence that no longer exists fails the sweep too, which
is what stops this file going stale the way the comments at the call sites did. Add `task` when the entry is an
adoption intended for later rather than a settled decision; it is then re-reported on every run.
`roles` names the file of this package each role resolves; the shared config is resolved for the same file.

script|no-console|level.why: The build, lint and version scripts are CLI entry points whose output IS their interface, so printing to stdout is what they are for. The shared config leaves the rule on because it is written for library code, which has no business printing.

script|no-restricted-syntax|option|optio.why: Same selector, same severity - the message names this package's own escape hatches (`strictProxy<T>()`, `ensureGenericObject()`), which the shared config does not know about and could not name.

script|unicorn/no-top-level-assignment-i.why: Module-level state written from a function is this package's registry / cache / once-guard pattern - `setTransportOptionsResolver`, the memoized transport, the once-flagged process-cleanup handler. Those shapes are production code here, so the rule is off over the whole tree rather than only where the shared config expects them.

script|unicorn/no-top-level-side-effects.why: Module-initialization side effects ARE the contract for this package's entry points: the framework setup modules register their context resolvers at import time, and the script entry points call `exitIfScriptDisabled()` before anything reads what they set up. Deferring them into a function would mean consumers had to call something extra, which is what these modules exist to avoid.

script|unicorn/prefer-group-by|level.why: `Map.groupBy` is ES2024 and this package's language floor is ES2022, beside the same block's `unicorn/prefer-array-from-async` relaxation for `Array.fromAsync`.
